actions: Continue the 20% peak café capacity reservation pilot in the 50 US cafés through February 2027, maintaining capped mobile slots and up to two additional peak staff-hours per weekday per pilot store.

Instrument all order attempts, slot offers, completions, refunds, staffing, and repeat purchases for paired measurement against 50 comparison cafés. No expansion or contraction of the pilot at this time.
moves.rationale: Starbucks’ incentives are to restore a credible coffeehouse visit without sacrificing digital convenience, defend transaction momentum, and earn back added labor through all-channel contribution. With the pilot just launched and no measured evidence yet on wait times, contribution, or repeat behavior, the strategic move is to hold the line on the pilot parameters, gather robust paired-store data, and avoid premature expansion, rollback, or pricing changes. This preserves optionality for March, ensures operational reversibility, and keeps within binding constraints (staffing, price, 50-store scope).
resource_commitments: Maintain up to two additional peak staff-hours per weekday per pilot store (maximum 2 hours x 5 days/week x 50 stores).
Dedicate analytics and operations resources to collect and analyze paired-store metrics (order attempts, completions, refunds, staffing, repeat purchases) through February.
expected_responses: Dunkin and Dutch Bros are likely to sustain or incrementally adjust their own local offers (e.g., breakfast bundles, mobile credits, peak labor) to capture redirected mobile demand, but will not escalate dramatically until Starbucks’ results are clearer.
Some mobile customers will continue to redirect to competitors or home preparation if Starbucks slots are unavailable; walk-in café customers will benefit from shorter waits.
Competitors may watch for evidence of Starbucks’ pilot success or failure before making larger moves.
